archetypes.name: cli-contract
archetypes.rationale: Large sh-to-py migration with ~40 new CLI verbs; KV key names, exit codes, and stdout/stderr routing must match the original bash scripts exactly — static panel doesn't compare against the bash contract.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every `*_main` function in the new `ci_cli.py`, `git_cli.py`, `gh_cli.py`, `merge_cli.py`, and `pr_cli.py` files. For each verb, check: (1) that KV keys emitted to stdout match the original bash script exactly (e.g., `RESULT` only on success in `sync_local_main_main`, `CLEAN`/`DIRTY_OUT`/`PROBE_ERROR` in `clean_tree_main`); (2) exit codes including usage exits match the plan's F13-r5 table (e.g., `merge_cli.pr_main` always returns 0 — is that correct given the plan says usage exit 1?); (3) `ci_cli.wait_main` catches all exceptions and returns 0 when `output_file` is set — determine whether this can silently suppress fatal errors in callers that rely on the exit code; (4) `behind_count_main` usage-exit-2 path is actually reachable (the `_parse` helper returns an int for bad argv, but `args.no_fetch` would only fail on argparse error — trace the path). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: regression-risk
archetypes.rationale: Several modifications to existing modules (ci_monitor.py, checks.py, finalize.py) make subtle behavioral changes that could silently break callers; the static panel may not identify these as cross-module regressions.
archetypes.prompt_body: Focus on places in modified (not new) files where observable behavior changed beyond the stated scope. Specifically: (1) `ci_monitor.py` `gather_status` exception path at line ~677 now returns `status="pending", conflicted=True` instead of the old `status="error"` — trace every caller of `gather_status` and `poll_ci` to determine whether any downstream decision branch breaks when `status="error"` is never returned from a PR-view failure; (2) `collect_failed_logs` in `ci_monitor.py` now returns partial text in both `in_progress` and `error` states — callers that previously got empty `text` on error now get redacted log text, which may change `_fix_exhausted_detail` formatting or Step 18a stall recovery routing; (3) `_fix_exhausted_detail` now calls `redact.redact(tail)` on text from `logs.text` which is already redacted by `collect_failed_logs` — verify whether double redaction is harmless or corrupts tokens like masked run-IDs; (4) `git.rebase_abort` always returns exit 0 even on failure — confirm this is idempotent intent, not a swallowed error. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
